# The EXPECTED.md claim census

*Generated by `node scripts/expected-claim-census.mjs`, against the sibling
revisions pinned in `test/fixtures/siblings.json` (`bw-board@a301937`,
`bw-circuit-ui@410f8ce`), on 2026-08-24. `test/expected-quantities-hold.test.mjs`
is the gate; this file is its report.*

Every unit-bearing number in every `examples/*/EXPECTED.md` is a CLAIM. This is
what happens to each of them.

- **checked** — compared against something that could have contradicted it: a
  solve of the authored `circuit.json` at the operating point the claim names, a
  value `circuit.json` declares, the program's own timeline, or the claim's own
  stated arithmetic.
- **skipped** — declined, with a reason. A declined claim is an UNVERIFIED
  claim, and the reason table says what the instrument could not do. It is not
  the same as a claim being wrong.
- **mismatched** — the engine contradicts it. Every one is recorded in
  `test/fixtures/expected-claim-exceptions.json` with a verdict naming which
  side is wrong; the gate fails on any that is not.

`node scripts/expected-claim-census.mjs <example>` prints one example claim by
claim, with the reason for each.

## Totals

| | engine | claims | compared | checked | mismatched | skipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before this sweep | bw-board@88e9668 | 2358 | 34 (1.4 %) | 34 | 0 | 2324 |
| after wave 1 | bw-board@88e9668 | 2358 | 1209 (51.3 %) | 1208 | 1 | 1149 |
| after wave 2 | bw-board@a301937 | 2356 | **1224 (52.0 %)** | 1223 | 1 | 1132 |
| the same, on the merged tree | bw-board@a301937 | 2392 | 1230 (51.4 %) | 1229 | 1 | 1162 |

The last row is wave 2 measured again after merging the lane that landed
43-rc-timing's repeatable step and pc50's in-range Bode bench: 36 more claims in
the denominator, 6 more compared. Both are kept, because only the `after wave 2`
row is a like-for-like measurement of what this wave did — a percentage that
moves because someone else added claims is not this wave's result either way.

Wave 2 is the `bw-board` pin bump from `88e9668` to `a301937`, and its +15 is a
net of two opposite movements that both belong in the record:

| | claims | why |
|---|---|---|
| +2 | 47-battery-led, pc32-pnp-high-side | the two ENGINE declines this gate recorded are gone: `vsource` honours `rInternal`, and a saturated PNP stamps its base junction again |
| +8 | 47-battery-led, 52-battery-voltage-divider, pc84-led-herz and 3 others | a markdown list item stopped inheriting the previous bullet's qualifier — a wrapped sentence continues on an unbulleted line, so two bullets are two statements |
| +8 | pc77, pc78, pc79, pc80 | the four German source-resistance lessons re-derived: their `## Meter readings (hand-computed)` heading was silencing the engine for the WHOLE SECTION, by a rule entirely separate from the rInternal decline |
| −3 | pc25-relay-isolator, pc28-logic-interlock, pc36-series-interlock | taken back OFF the checked pile: they were passing against a bench that reports no current at all |

Two repairs came out of the mutation proof rather than out of the sweep, and
both are worth reading:

- **A net's throughput was double-counted.** `bench-measure.mjs` summed the
  POSITIVE terminal currents on a net, but the engine's sign is a property of
  the part, not of the node: `resistor_7.b = +12.0113 mA` and
  `led_5.anode = +12.0113 mA` are the same 12 mA seen from both ends, and the
  measurand reported 24.0226 mA of throughput through a branch carrying 12.
  That phantom is what let the mutation escape — pc78's original, wrong
  `I = 9 / 412 = 21.8 mA` agreed with 24.0226 inside the 10 % band, so
  reinstating the defect this wave repaired left the suite GREEN. Half the sum
  of the magnitudes is the throughput at any node where KCL holds, whatever the
  sign convention.
- **pc11-direct-parallel shipped a bench that contradicts its own lesson.**
  Removing the phantom surfaced it. `intro.md` says "Both light up at the same
  brightness", tells the reader to "check that both LEDs show the same voltage
  and current", and gives 6.4 mA each for 12.8 mA total — while the bench
  declared `led_4` red at Vf 2.0 and `led_5` **blue at Vf 3.1**, so the two
  branches carried 6.2500 mA and 3.9583 mA and the total was 10.21 mA. Step 1
  of "Try this" fails on the shipped circuit. The lesson is right and the bench
  was wrong; `led_5` is now a red LED at Vf 2.0 and both branches carry
  6.2500 mA for 12.5000 mA total. Same class as pc07-pot-dimmer and
  44-darlington-motor in the previous wave: a document that was correct about a
  circuit nobody had built.

The −3 is the one to read twice. A claim of "0 mA" on a bench whose every
branch current reads 0.0000 mA passes for the wrong reason — it would pass with
the lamp blazing. Counting it as coverage was this gate measuring the absence of
an instrument. `test/device-branch-agreement.test.mjs` names the two benches
that are in that state (168p01-blink and avr01-blink, of the 69 a current claim
reaches) so the decline cannot outlive its subject.

The 34 is not a slur on the previous gate: it read three hand-written shapes out
of the prose — a frequency beside a period, a `Frequency:` beside a two-wait
program, and at most ONE current bullet per example — and read them well. It had
no denominator, so nobody could see what it was not reading.

The one mismatch is `arduino-sk-p04-color-mixing`, whose page describes three
pots, three resistors and an RGB LED over a bench holding one pot and nothing
else. It is one of fourteen stubbed `arduino-sk-*` benches, which is why it is
recorded with a verdict rather than repaired.

## Why a claim was not compared

| n | why a claim was not compared |
|---|---|
| 189 | condition label — the leading cell of a table row states the operating point the rest of the row answers for |
| 148 | counterfactual or comparative prose — the number is stated about a bench other than this one, or is a rating rather than a measurement |
| 143 | a component value outside ## Circuit — a what-if row, a derived total, or a value named in passing, not a statement about this bench |
| 102 | no authored circuit.json to hold the declared value against |
| 77 | no authored circuit.json to hold the claim against |
| 70 | a frequency with no period stated beside it and no two-wait program to derive one from |
| 69 | the example has no program.bw waits to hold a duration against |
| 53 | a tone the firmware commands — this gate does not run firmware, and the bench has no oscillator whose frequency it could read instead |
| 46 | the operating point is a SEQUENCE of control changes against the clock (the document states it as an audit-solve --set invocation), and this gate solves at one point rather than scripting a run |
| 43 | a percentage outside a table — a duty cycle or a proportion this gate does not derive |
| 43 | a duration the program does not wait — it names an observation instant or a time constant, which this checker does not derive |
| 28 | the operating point is named by the COLUMN header rather than the row, and this gate reads conditions from rows |
| 20 | a percentage with no voltage beside it in the row to be a percentage OF |
| 20 | free-running oscillator — the claim is about a waveform and a solve is an instant |
| 19 | driven bench — the source is a waveform, so a solve is an instant |
| 17 | the row puts two switches in different states, and this gate drives every switch on a bench together |
| 14 | the sentence states both switch states at once, so no single operating point is the one it is claiming about |
| 13 | temp claims have no derivation here — nothing in the engine reads a temperature or a magnetic quantity back |
| 10 | a PWM or servo pulse duty — a firmware-generated waveform, not a shape this gate reads from the program's waits |
| 9 | the bench is driven by a module whose output level is an input this gate cannot set |
| 5 | the bench solves for node voltages but every branch current on it reads exactly 0 A — the elements are dropping volts, so current is flowing and the engine simply has no readback for it here; a gap in the instrument, not a defect in the document, and a claim of 0 mA would pass against it just as wrongly |
| 5 | a percentage of a step or of a remaining distance, not of the rail — the reference it is a percentage OF is itself a solved quantity this gate does not re-derive |
| 4 | a duty cycle on an example whose program states no waits |
| 3 | a percentage of a rail the bench does not declare |
| 2 | a time constant on a bench with no single capacitor to take R x C from |
| 2 | the bench declares no ohm — the document names a component the bench does not have |
| 2 | the operating point is a PWM duty cycle, which is a firmware state this gate does not run |
| 2 | the document divides by led1's DECLARED forward drop of 2.1 V — the ideal-model answer — while the engine's junction solves to 2.214 V here; a model difference, not a document defect, and the line's own arithmetic is what this gate holds it to |
| 1 | a duty cycle on a program driving 2 outputs — the lit time this gate tracks is their union, not the one lamp the claim is about |
| 1 | a headroom reference — the number is on the far side of a "<<" or ">>" comparison, so it is the ceiling the measured value is being held against rather than a measurement of this bench |
| 1 | the document divides by led1's DECLARED forward drop of 2 V — the ideal-model answer — while the engine's junction solves to 2.118 V here; a model difference, not a document defect, and the line's own arithmetic is what this gate holds it to |
| 1 | the document divides by led1's DECLARED forward drop of 2.1 V — the ideal-model answer — while the engine's junction solves to 2.147 V here; a model difference, not a document defect, and the line's own arithmetic is what this gate holds it to |
